source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Settings" -> Click tab "SSL Settings" -> Click " Generate CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT" .
SSL Certificate key will be changed
View ssl certificate match your modified settings.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Result should be human readable.
Login BMC web successfully.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl + jq, openssl (user-supplied cert for upload)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Generate CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT: generates a new HTTPS/SSL certificate (write to the BMC key/cert store); it is a security-sensitive state change + (for upload) needs the cert file. Agent can help with the generate/upload request once the user supplies the CSR settings/cert, then verify: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol/HTTPS/Certificates 2>&1 | jq .
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish certificate-list JSON after the generate/upload so the user confirms the new certificate is present/active.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: generating/uploading a certificate changes the BMC HTTPS trust/identity and can disrupt management connections; do only with user-provided values and verify connectivity after.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes key/certificate state and access risk, but conflates the source Generate action with upload, asks for a user-supplied certificate that may be irrelevant, guesses a resource path, uses insecure verification and only lists metadata. It does not prove BMC key generation, exact parameters, activation, served identity, private-key non-exportability or WebUI login.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires owner parameters, secure key handling, pre/post certificate baseline, bounded reconnect, served-chain validation and recovery. V3.1 narrows this row to generation semantics—self-signed certificate or CSR/key generation as defined by firmware—and keeps the next upload row independent.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 924/2291 accepts a generate/upload prose path without resolving generation mode, key algorithm, subject/SAN, active slot, activation/restart, old-certificate recovery or actual served/WebUI evidence.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The preceding View row is read-only and the following Upload row accepts supplied certificate material. Neither proves the BMC-generated key/certificate or CSR behavior required here.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1086, Wistron-BMC-00215-V002 or c6011334a7b8b7ff draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves Generate and key-change semantics; ED-34 treats generation mode/parameters/activation as Project inputs; ED-35 retains actual generation and login rather than list-only evidence; ED-38 requires approval, recovery, one attempt and no automatic retry.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC WebUI Generate Certificate Management function creates a new BMC-held private key and corresponding self-signed certificate or CSR according to the firmware/Project generation mode, displays the resulting identity readably, activates the intended certificate state and preserves approved WebUI access.
original_method: Baseline the active certificate/chain/fingerprint, slots and trusted recovery access; define the source generation mode and approved subject/SAN/key/validity parameters; invoke the exact WebUI Generate action once after confirmation; capture its UI/audit/key-identity result, monitor any HTTPS restart, prove a new public key/fingerprint and intended active/pending state, validate the served identity/chain and perform a fresh WebUI login through the approved trust path without exporting the private key.
manual_activity: An engineer defines whether firmware generates a self-signed certificate or CSR/key pair, approves all identity/cryptographic parameters and the HTTPS access outage/recovery. A human invokes and visually checks the source WebUI action and performs fresh login. Automation can validate public metadata and served state, but cannot expose private keys, substitute upload or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware/WebUI identity and vendor definition of the Generate control/output
Approved management DNS name/IP and subject/CN/SAN/organization/country/email fields
Key algorithm/size/curve, signature algorithm, validity and key-usage policy
Current active certificate/chain/fingerprint/public key/slot and trusted client baseline
Expected activation/restart/session effect and reconnect deadline
Independent recovery and old-certificate/factory restoration method
WebUI field readability, served identity/trust and fresh-login acceptance
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/security/audit logs or collect/export the generated private key, password, token or other secret in artifacts.
Verify exact target, generation mode and approved identity/crypto parameters before the WebUI action; do not upload a certificate or combine the next case.
Preserve pre-change public metadata and recovery, but do not assume the old private key can or should be exported; ensure vendor-supported rollback exists.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one generation only. Do not repeatedly generate keys or delete/overwrite additional slots on timeout.
Do not use `curl -k` or a resource listing as trust proof. Verify the new public key/fingerprint, served chain, hostname/SAN and explicit trust outcome.
Stop on wrong identity/algorithm/slot, failed activation, reconnect timeout or lost WebUI/API; use independent recovery and approved rollback without another blind generation.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, generation mode, approved parameters, baseline, slot/activation/reconnect behavior, recovery and visual/login evidence; present exact WebUI action for confirmation.
After human invokes Generate once, capture UI/audit result and public certificate/CSR metadata, proving the public key/fingerprint changes as expected without private-key exposure.
Monitor bounded HTTPS/BMC recovery, collect complete management/served certificate state and perform the approved fresh WebUI login/trust check.
Archive redacted evidence and stop without upload substitution, insecure verification, automatic generation/retry, certificate deletion or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve generation mode and exact identity/cryptographic/validity/slot parameters plus private-key handling expectations.
Approve the one-time WebUI action, service/session impact, recovery/rollback and trust/login acceptance.
Review UI/audit, new public-key/certificate or CSR, activation/served chain and access evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Only describes risk and a readback. Requiring an upload certificate conflates the next case, the generic resource may be wrong, `-k` defeats trust and a list cannot prove key generation, parameter match, activation, served identity or login.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact vendor WebUI Generate control with approved generation fields once. Use protected discovered API and verified TLS tools only for public metadata/active-state corroboration; never export the BMC-generated private key.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Settings > SSL Settings > Generate Certificate Management path, explicit key-change statement, match-modified-settings/readability/login Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek proposal/risk and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not turn Generate into Upload.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run one parameter-controlled BMC-side generation, prove a new protected key/public identity, activation and verified served certificate, then confirm fresh WebUI access with independent recovery available.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC firmware's Certificate Management Generate function and approved management PKI/trust path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/WebUI/Redfish/TLS client versions, crypto policy and trust bundle.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor certificate-generation/CSR/key-store/activation specification, Project PKI/TLS policy and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes generation mode, fields, key evidence, activation, trust and recovery measurable while retaining the source WebUI and login checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Upload is a different row; CSR generation does not prove self-signed activation unless required; metadata list does not prove served identity or login; API generation does not automatically prove WebUI control.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Generation mode/parameters, current state, slot/activation, trust, reconnect and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A bad generated identity can break hostname trust and management access; repeated generation can destroy recoverable key/cert state; CSR-only output may require a later signed-upload workflow.

project_override_considerations: A Project may approve a vendor API/tool for generation only if the original WebUI path, actual method, reason, engineer approval, key-generation equivalence and uncovered UI coverage are recorded. A supplied-certificate upload is not an equivalent override and must remain the next case.
expected_evidence: Target/version/endpoint identity, approved generation mode/fields/crypto policy, pre-change active chain/fingerprint/public key/slot and independent recovery approval
WebUI Generate screenshots/audit and returned self-signed certificate or CSR/public-key metadata without private-key material
Proof public key/fingerprint and intended slot/pending/active state changed exactly once with activation/reconnect timeline
Verified served full chain, hostname/SAN/validity/key usage/trust result and human-readable WebUI field match
Fresh WebUI/API login through approved trust path, preserved rollback state/no retry/private-key exposure and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe BMC-side certificate generation, changed key, readable modified settings and successful WebUI login. Whether the product generates self-signed certificate versus CSR/key pair is a firmware/Project readiness input, not a competing source purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The generation and post-access objective are identifiable. Vendor documentation and Project PKI inputs can define mode, parameters, activation and recovery, so execution is pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but separates Generate from Upload, rejects list-only/insecure proof and adds key-generation, activation, trust and fresh-login evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on critical certificate controls and sharpens generation-mode/output and private-key non-exportability rather than a generic generate/upload path.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces conditional prose with a one-generation state transition and independent served/access verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Preserves View as read-only and Upload as supplied-material replacement; neither substitutes for BMC-generated key evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an insecure post-list or unrelated upload from being reported as successful BMC key/certificate generation and protects management access and private-key secrecy through one-shot recovery-aware verification.
independent_technical_reasoning: The defining event is creation of a new key pair inside the BMC. A changed certificate list alone can result from upload or metadata refresh and does not establish private-key generation, parameter correctness or active serving. The evidence must bind the WebUI Generate action to a new public key/fingerprint, documented key storage, activation and a verified login, while recovery is arranged before the HTTPS identity changes.
